orig:
Announcements
October 28, 2026
Inside the Three New AI innovations in Ads Ranking Improving your Ad Performance
Last year, we took you behind the scenes of Meta's ads ranking systems and showed you four AI innovations that are driving advertiser performance.
Since then, we’ve continued innovating. We've been rebuilding and evolving the systems that decide which ads get considered, how well their performance is predicted, and how quickly a brand-new ad can start working for you. These innovations apply to your ads automatically, improving your performance without you having to tune your campaigns.
In the second quarter of 2026, improvements to Meta's ads ranking system drove an 8.3% more ad clicks and a 15.7% uplift in conversions on Facebook and are part of our broader ads delivery system.
This year, the AI behind Meta ads got better at three specific jobs. It considers more of the ads you've made. It predicts better across every app, surface and objective at once. And it leverages LLMs to understand what your ad is about while remembering how people responded to your ad in the past.
Here are three AI innovations across our ads systems that are driving advertiser performance:
1. Meta Andromeda: The Concierge Who Now Expertly Considers Each Ad
Meta Andromeda is our ads retrieval engine — the first step in the ranking process, where we narrow a pool of tens of millions of ads down to the shortlist we consider showing someone. When we introduced it in 2024, Andromeda was about depth: an end-to-end hardware, software and machine learning co-designed system, built with Meta Training and Inference Accelerator (MTIA) and NVIDIA Grace Hopper Superchip, that enabled a 10,000x increase in the complexity of the models used for retrieval.
The next generation of Andromeda, co-designed again with NVIDIA, is about smarter breadth. Rather than running one general model across everything, Andromeda now routes each ad to specialized "expert" models — which means it brings near ranking-level judgment into the retrieval stage. In production, the system scores every eligible ad and surfaces the top candidates at over one billion ads per second, a new throughput benchmark for ads retrieval-stage models. A better shortlist at the start shows up later as more clicks and conversions for your business.
Said differently: In 2025, we described Andromeda as a personal concierge who knows your tastes so well they don't just know you covet shoes — they know you like red flip flops at the beach. That concierge is still there. What's changed is that they now walk the entire store. Before, they'd check the most popular shelves, the ones they knew best. Now they read every product label on every shelf, in the same amount of time, and bring back a better group of products you actually want.
For your business, this means that more of your ads, creative variations and products are considered for each person— more shelves read in the same instant, and a better chance the right one reaches the person it suits best.
Results: Since 2025, Meta Andromeda has delivered a 2.4% increase in conversions on Facebook. In Q3, we increased the complexity of Andromeda by 10X without increasing computing costs or hardware needs. These improvements increased conversions by 1.37% on Facebook and 0.24% on Instagram Reels.
2. Meta GEM: The Super Brain That Now Teaches the Whole Class
When we introduced GEM — our industry leading Generative Ads Recommendation Model — in March 2025, it was a new model trained on thousands of GPUs at LLM scale, and it had just launched on Facebook Feed and Instagram, where it increased ad conversions by up to 5% in a short few months.
GEM is no longer a pioneering effort on a few surfaces. It’s now the foundation model behind ads recommendations across Facebook, Instagram, Reels and off-Meta-conversions, trained at the scale of a large language model, and it works for every major advertiser goal — from website conversions to mobile app installs. And it doesn't just serve your ads directly. Instead, GEM teaches the models that do so through state-of-art innovations in knowledge transfer — passing down what it learns centrally and its historical memory to the models that rank ads in real time, across every surface and every objective.
Campaigns with few conversions now benefit from what GEM learns about other clicks data, so advertisers with deep-funnel objectives gain better performance. The new generation of GEM understands each user’s ads engagement better and matches ads more accurately — reading 2x longer engagement history through a 2.5x more complex model with deep co-design with the latest hardware trained across thousands of latest-generation GPUs. Instead of each surface and each funnel stage improving on its own timeline, the improvements hit every surface at once.
Said differently: In 2025, we compared GEM to a super brain that could read an entire library in seconds and connect every detail. It still can. Now that super brain learns from signals across Meta's ads platforms, works out what's generally true about how people move toward a purchase, and then trains many specialist ads ranking models that are doing the real-time work of matching your ad to the right person. You don't just talk to the professor. You get the benefit of everyone they taught collaborating.
Results: Since 2025, GEM has delivered up to a 18.9% conversion improvement and a 12% ad click-through rate improvement across Meta's ad surfaces and objectives. Additionally, it contributed 5.8%, 4.1%, and 1.6% conversion uplift on Facebook, Instagram, and offsite conversions for targeted users. These gains span both upper-funnel surfaces and deep-funnel optimization goals, driving stronger results for advertisers.
3. Meta GenRecs: A New Way To Reason and Recommend Ads — Starting With The Shared Language
Our state-of-the-art ads recommendation systems answer one question extremely well: how likely is this person to click or convert on a given ad? Meta Generative Recommender, GenRecs for short, further improves those predictions by enriching LLM models with world and ad-ecosystem knowledge. Now the LLM can reason about ad content and user preferences together, predicting the most relevant ad for each person, even with brand-new ads with little engagement history.
We are enriching the ad recommendation system through a set of connected innovations, end-to-end optimization, rather than a single launch. It begins with GenRecs Tokenization: large language models read each ad's text and images and describe the ad in semantic tokens that capture its key attributes — a product's brand, color, fit and style. Those semantic tokens form a shared vocabulary that lets a model relate an item with limited engagement history to items it knows well, and improves the performance for newer ads.
That shared vocabulary now sits underneath our ranking models, and it is what generative retrieval runs on. Retrieval is the first stage of ads recommendation, narrowing millions of candidates down to a few thousand before ranking models make the final selection. GenRecs now enriches Andromeda, our existing retrieval model: it generates the semantic ID for the ideal ad for a person, then matches that to the ads available in our system.
For your business, this means new ads, refreshed creative and new products get on a faster track to performing— because the system can understand them through what it already knows about similar ads and products, whether the signals are plentiful or more limited. And as the system reasons more about what people actually want, we can reach someone who's in the market for what you sell, even when nothing in their past clicks looks like your ad.
Said differently: Imagine a library where the librarians already know the popular books well, from catalog cards and years of records of who borrows what. Tokenization adds shared subject words the whole library uses, so a newly released book that arrived this morning is already categorized with everything else we know. Retrieval is where this starts to pay off. Out of millions of books, the librarian looks at the subjects you have borrowed before and what you want today, then names the subject you will want next — in the way a language model predicts the next word. She then finds the closest books— even if one just arrived in the library and it has no prior borrow history.
Results: In the third quarter of 2026 we expanded GenRecs to generative retrieval on Facebook Feed, increasing conversions by nearly +2% across targeted segments. And paired with Meta's GEM and Meta's Adaptive Ranking Model, GenRecs Tokenization has delivered a +0.35% lift in conversions across surfaces for advertisers.
What this means for the people who see your ads
Better retrieval, better prediction and better understanding aren't only an advertiser story. They’re a story of better experiences for people who see ads. They help us show people ads that are more relevant to what they're interested in.
What you can do about it
Every one of these improvements reaches your account automatically. There's no setting to switch on, no new campaign type to adopt, no migration to plan. They're already in the system that's delivering your ads today.
How much you get out of them still depends on what you give the system to work with: the outcomes you tell it to optimize for, the quality of the data you share - including how you measure performance, and how much of the optimization you let the models handle.
The Meta Ads system is getting better at understanding people’s interests, products and services. It still needs you to tell it what winning looks like for your business.

orig:
Announcements
October 28, 2026
How Meta's Ads System Matches Your Ad to the Right Person at the Right Time
Takeaways
- We regularly improve Meta's ads system and AI models on the backend, and those updates automatically roll out to your campaigns.
- The highest bid or the biggest budget doesn't automatically win in the auction.
- Ad quality reflects the whole customer experience, including what happens after the click.
- You control the outcome you optimize for, what each conversion is worth, and how results are measured.
Our ads system is a market, where there is a limited number of opportunities to auction impressions. Our goal is to maximize the long-term value for advertisers, while promoting a high-trust and high-quality ecosystem for people and businesses.
Advertisers set the strategy, budget and goal to guide the ads system to delivering results that matter to their business. Behind the scenes, machine learning and AI models retrieve, rank and recommend an ad based on things like where a person may be in their shopping journey and their willingness to convert, as well as the content of an ad and the purchase experience of prior purchasers.
Your ad then competes in the auction with other eligible ads for every available impression where we predict the cost per outcome is lower than what you are willing to pay. This happens hundreds of billions of times a day, across Facebook, Instagram, Threads, Messenger, WhatsApp, and Audience Network, drawing on what the 3.64 billion people using at least one of our apps each day show us they care about.1
The ads system does this measurably better than in 2025 with the proliferation of AI enhancements. In Q2 2026 alone, advances in our user-understanding models — combined with our Generative Ads Recommendation Model (GEM) and sequence learning — delivered an 8.3% increase in ad clicks and a 15.7% uplift in conversions on Facebook.2 Meta Generative Recommender or GenRecs, which uses LLMs to reason across ad content and user preferences to predict the best ad for each person, was also introduced in Q2 2026. In Q3, we launched generative retrieval on Facebook Feed, driving a nearly 2% increase in conversions across targeted segments. And we continue to scale our retrieval systems efficiently. In Q3, improvements to Andromeda including scaling model complexity and throughput increased conversions by 1.4% on Facebook.3
How AI Finds the Right Ad for Each Person
Here's how it works: imagine a personal shopper with thirty seconds to find something for you. In the past, they only had time to check brands you’ve previously interacted with, products adjacent to the ones you’ve purchased before, or popular products. Now your shopper can scan every product in the store. Then imagine that the personal shopper increasingly utilizes what they know about your preferred fit, style and what you tend to buy, to narrow down the best option even further. And they know you have a ski trip coming up and bought boots yesterday, so they bring you a ski jacket, not a second pair of boots. If you're the brand, your jacket was hanging at the back of the store. It may have been overlooked. Now it gets found by the person who is actively looking for something just like it.
Each part of that maps to our ads system:
- Scanning every product is Meta Andromeda, our retrieval system. It narrows tens of millions of ads to the few thousand worth ranking for each person.4
- Knowing your preferences, preferred size and style is Meta GEM, the state-of-the-art, largest foundation model for recommendation systems in the industry.5 GEM learns from trillions of signals and shares what it learns with the smaller models that choose ads in real time.6
- Knowing what comes next is sequence learning, which reads the order of what someone does. In this case, this is the personal shopper knowing that once you book the ski trip, you may be in the market for new gear.
- Meta Lattice ties it together as one ranking system that learns across advertiser goals and across our apps, instead of a separate model and data for each. Think of this like all of the knowledge inside the head of your personal shopper, who can put all the various pieces together to make decisions about what to consider buying next.
These gains build on each other, and they reach your account with no work from you. As the ads system gets better at finding people likely to act, each impression drives more results — which is one reason demand in the auction keeps growing.
How the Auction Determines Which Ad Is Shown
Every ad participates in an auction before it's shown, competing in real time against other eligible ads. The auction balances three entities: people who should see relevant ads, advertisers who need results, and Meta’s commitment to a high trust ecosystem that has to stay healthy for both. The highest bid or the biggest budget doesn't automatically win, quality of ad experience, purchase experience, and product satisfaction matter too.
Three of the main inputs are below — the first two are shaped by your choices, and the third is where our AI does the work:
- Your Bid: What you're willing to pay for this opportunity. We turn your budget and goals into a bid for each impression, continually adjusted to maximize your results within your budget or cost constraints. These adjustments are called pacing and are based on live market conditions.
- Ad Quality: The quality of the whole experience, from the ad itself to what happens after the click. It reflects feedback from people who view, click or hide ads, detection of low-quality traits such as engagement bait or withheld information, and more than 200 million customer survey responses a year covering satisfaction with purchases, shipping delays, unexpected charges, and whether people felt misled.7
- Estimated Action Rate: State-of-the-art machine learning model prediction that this person will take the action you're asking the system to optimize for.
A more relevant ad, backed by a better customer experience, can beat a higher bid. For more detail, see About ad auctions in the Business Help Center.
Get Better Results by Telling the System What You Value
Every business is unique in what it needs in the current moment. The improvements we've made to our ads system make it better at delivering the specific outcomes that matter to your business. But our platform can only optimize for the objectives you tell it. For example, do you care about driving as many sales as possible, or would you rather focus on a specific type of sale, such as one from a new customer? Three decisions set your results apart:
- The Goal: Choose the outcome you actually want, not the closest proxy you can measure. A lead isn't a sale, and an install isn't a subscriber.
- What It's Worth: Send back the value of each conversion, not just the fact that a conversion happened, so delivery weights toward your most valuable outcomes. Set a goal-based bid and turn on Value Optimization and Value Rules to steer the ad system toward the conversions or customers that are most valuable to your business.
- How It's Measured: Optimize to the measurement you trust: Meta's measurement using standard attribution, your own attribution framework using custom attribution, or incrementality experiments with incremental attribution, conversions that would not have happened without the ad.
Tips for Your Next Campaign
We expect our ads system to continue improving, and these improvements will reach your campaigns automatically. The most useful steps you can take are ones that help it work better for your business:
- Give the system room to work. Adopt Meta Advantage+ rather than component by component, and supply more creative variety so the system has more to test and learn from.
- Judge results on cost per result or return on ad spend, and test incrementality. Platform-reported results show what happened; a Conversion Lift or Brand Lift study shows what happened because of your ads.
- Audit your customer experience. Shipping speed, support responsiveness, product quality and checkout friction impact ad quality. Review them the way you review creative.
- Plan for your peak seasons. Protect budget for the windows when your customers are most ready to buy, and use budget scheduling to grow or shift spend automatically.
